punchline: Soft as water, determined enough to pierce stone.
thirty_sec: Compiled in China roughly twenty-four centuries ago, the Tao Te Ching makes an unusual claim about power across its eighty-one short chapters: nothing in the world is softer than water. This tiny text has inspired leadership, strategy, art and everyday life for more than two thousand years, and it remains one of the most translated books in the entire world.
question: Which problem could you solve by reading its current instead of forcing it?
key_contrast: The hard breaks; the soft wears through and wins.
